# Practical 1 - Using R and RStudio

::: {.callout-tip .partmenu #parts-0100}

## Practical 1 - Using R and RStudio

### @sec-p1_r_and_rstudio

#### Sections

- @sec-open_r
- @sec-r_language
- @sec-coding_in_the_console
- @sec-rstudio_interface
- @sec-console_scripts

#### Learning Objectives

By the end of this part of the practical you should be able to:

- Explain what R is and why it is useful for biological data analysis.
- Use some features of the RStudio interface.
- Use the R console and R scripts to run R code.

### @sec-p2_quarto

#### Sections

- @sec-quarto
- @sec-formatting_quarto
- @sec-analysis_in_quarto
- @sec-documenting_and_formatting_your_code
- @sec-advanced_quarto_formatting

#### Learning Objectives

By the end of this part of the practical you should be able to:

- Use Quarto documents to run R code.
- Create a simple reproducible analysis using Quarto.
- Explain the benefits of writing clear, well-formatted and documented R code.

### @sec-p3_functions_and_variables

#### Sections

- @sec-functions
- @sec-arguments
- @sec-variables
- @sec-variable_types
- @sec-r_quirks

#### Learning Objectives

By the end of this part of the practical you should be able to:

- Explain what a function is and use simple functions.
- Explain the purpose of function arguments and provide arguments to functions.
- Explain what a variable is and create and use variables in R.
- Recognise and use common variable types, including numeric, character and logical variables.

### @sec-p4_vectors_data_frames_plots

#### Sections

- @sec-packages
- @sec-vectors
- @sec-data_frames
- @sec-csv
- @sec-plots

#### Learning Objectives

By the end of this part of the practical you should be able to:

- Install and load a package in R.
- Recognise and use the vector variable type.
- Isolate elements of the vector using an index.
- Create and view a simple data frame.
- Recognise and use the CSV file type.
- Plot a simple scatter plot in R.

:::
